yesno.quote: By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion.
yesno.note: Bible: Psalm 137:1. Boney M's disco hit "Rivers of Babylon" (1978) took its words from this psalm.

yesno.quote: She's buying a stairway to heaven.
yesno.note: Not the Bible: Led Zeppelin's "Stairway to Heaven" (1971). Jacob dreamed of a ladder to heaven in Genesis 28:12.

yesno.quote: A time to love, and a time to hate; a time of war, and a time of peace.
yesno.note: Bible: Ecclesiastes 3:8. The Byrds sang it in "Turn! Turn! Turn!", Pete Seeger's song built from Ecclesiastes 3.

yesno.quote: And what rough beast, its hour come round at last, slouches towards Bethlehem to be born?
yesno.note: Not the Bible: the last lines of W. B. Yeats's poem "The Second Coming" (1920).

yesno.quote: They shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid.
yesno.note: Bible: Micah 4:4. George Washington loved this verse, and Hamilton's "One Last Time" quotes it.

yesno.quote: God, grant me the serenity to accept the things I cannot change.
yesno.source: Serenity Prayer, usually credited to Reinhold Niebuhr (c. 1932); popular wording, authorship has been questioned
yesno.note: Not the Bible: the Serenity Prayer, usually credited to theologian Reinhold Niebuhr, from the 1930s.

yesno.quote: Let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.
yesno.note: Bible: Amos 5:24. Martin Luther King Jr. echoed it: "until justice rolls down like waters".

yesno.quote: What we do in life echoes in eternity.
yesno.note: Not the Bible: Maximus (Russell Crowe) in Gladiator (2000).

yesno.quote: Every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain and hill shall be made low.
yesno.note: Bible: Isaiah 40:4. Sung in Handel's Messiah and quoted in MLK's "I Have a Dream" speech.

yesno.quote: It's a cold and it's a broken Hallelujah.
yesno.note: Not the Bible: Leonard Cohen's "Hallelujah" (1984). The song name-checks David and Samson.

yesno.quote: I have been a stranger in a strange land.
yesno.note: Bible: Exodus 2:22, Moses naming his son. Heinlein's novel title "Stranger in a Strange Land" comes from it.

yesno.quote: With malice toward none; with charity for all.
yesno.note: Not the Bible: Abraham Lincoln's Second Inaugural Address (1865), a speech full of Bible quotes.

yesno.quote: How are the mighty fallen!
yesno.note: Bible: 2 Samuel 1:19, David's lament for Saul and Jonathan. Sounds like a headline or a movie line.

yesno.quote: Morning has broken like the first morning.
yesno.source: Cat Stevens, "Morning Has Broken" (1971); words by Eleanor Farjeon (1931)
yesno.note: Not the Bible: Eleanor Farjeon's 1931 hymn, made a pop hit by Cat Stevens (1971). It echoes Genesis 1.

yesno.quote: Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.
yesno.note: Bible: Psalm 30:5. Sounds like a soul or gospel lyric, but it is a psalm of David.

yesno.quote: Go placidly amid the noise and haste, and remember what peace there may be in silence.
yesno.note: Not the Bible: Max Ehrmann's prose poem "Desiderata" (1927), long wrongly said to be found in an old church.

yesno.quote: There is no new thing under the sun.
yesno.note: Bible: Ecclesiastes 1:9. Usually quoted as "nothing new under the sun".

yesno.quote: It is always darkest just before the day dawneth.
yesno.source: Thomas Fuller, A Pisgah-Sight of Palestine (1650)
yesno.note: Not the Bible: English preacher Thomas Fuller, 1650. The "-eth" is his, not King James's.

yesno.quote: Can two walk together, except they be agreed?
yesno.note: Bible: Amos 3:3. Sounds like a love-song lyric, but it is a prophet's question.

yesno.quote: Heaven has no rage like love to hatred turned, nor hell a fury like a woman scorned.
yesno.note: Not the Bible: William Congreve's play The Mourning Bride (1697), source of "Hell hath no fury".

yesno.quote: Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.
yesno.note: Bible: Ecclesiastes 4:9. Boys Like Girls and Taylor Swift had a 2009 hit called "Two Is Better Than One".

yesno.quote: There is no rest for the wicked.
yesno.note: Not the Bible as worded. Isaiah 57:21 says "There is no peace, saith my God, to the wicked."

yesno.quote: Let us eat and drink; for to morrow we shall die.
yesno.note: Bible: Isaiah 22:13. Sounds like a party anthem; the prophet was condemning that attitude.

yesno.quote: There will be an answer, let it be.
yesno.note: Not the Bible: The Beatles' "Let It Be" (1970). McCartney wrote it after dreaming of his late mother, Mary.

yesno.quote: What hath God wrought!
yesno.note: Bible: Numbers 23:23. Samuel Morse sent it as the first long-distance telegraph message (1844).

yesno.quote: I once was lost, but now am found, was blind, but now I see.
yesno.note: Not the Bible: John Newton's hymn "Amazing Grace". It echoes John 9:25: "whereas I was blind, now I see".

yesno.quote: His enemies shall lick the dust.
yesno.note: Bible: Psalm 72:9. Sounds like a heavy metal lyric, written about 3,000 years ago.

yesno.quote: All we are is dust in the wind.
yesno.note: Not the Bible: Kansas, "Dust in the Wind" (1977). It sounds like Ecclesiastes, but it is a rock ballad.

options.quote: Love is strong as death; jealousy is cruel as the grave.
Death cannot stop true love. All it can do is delay it for a while.
options.source: The Princess Bride (1987), spoken by Westley

options.quote: Love is not love which alters when it alteration finds.
The greatest thing you'll ever learn is just to love and be loved in return.

choose.note: Bible: Song of Solomon 8:6, older than The Princess Bride or Shakespeare. 'Love and be loved' is the song 'Nature Boy'.

options.quote: Love is a battlefield.
Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it.
My bounty is as boundless as the sea, my love as deep.
options.source: William Shakespeare, Romeo and Juliet, Act 2 Scene 2 (c. 1595)

options.quote: River deep, mountain high.
options.source: Ike & Tina Turner, "River Deep - Mountain High" (1966)

choose.note: Bible: Song of Solomon 8:7. Four love-and-water lines; the others are Pat Benatar, Juliet and Ike & Tina Turner.

options.quote: All you need is love.
options.source: The Beatles, "All You Need Is Love" (1967)

options.quote: How do I love thee? Let me count the ways.
options.source: Elizabeth Barrett Browning, Sonnets from the Portuguese, Sonnet 43 (1850)

options.quote: She walks in beauty, like the night of cloudless climes and starry skies.
My beloved is mine, and I am his.

choose.note: Bible: Song of Solomon 2:16. It sounds like a pop chorus; 'How do I love thee' is Elizabeth Barrett Browning.

options.quote: O, beware, my lord, of jealousy; it is the green-eyed monster which doth mock the meat it feeds on.
Jealousy is the rage of a man.
Love hurts.
Yet each man kills the thing he loves.
options.source: Oscar Wilde, The Ballad of Reading Gaol (1898)

choose.note: Bible: Proverbs 6:34. The archaic one is Iago in Othello; 'Each man kills the thing he loves' is Oscar Wilde.

options.quote: Sometimes it lasts in love, but sometimes it hurts instead.
'Tis better to have loved and lost than never to have loved at all.
There is a crack in everything, that's how the light gets in.
Even in laughter the heart is sorrowful; and the end of that mirth is heaviness.

choose.note: Bible: Proverbs 14:13. Sounds like a sad-clown soul song, written centuries before Adele or Leonard Cohen.

options.quote: Stolen waters are sweet, and bread eaten in secret is pleasant.
I can resist everything except temptation.
options.source: Oscar Wilde, Lady Windermere's Fan, Act 1 (1892), spoken by Lord Darlington

options.quote: You're the devil in disguise.
options.source: Elvis Presley, "(You're the) Devil in Disguise" (1963)

options.quote: He did not want the apple for the apple's sake, he wanted it only because it was forbidden.

choose.note: Bible: Proverbs 9:17, spoken by 'a foolish woman' tempting passers-by. The others are Wilde, Elvis and Twain.

options.quote: Bright star, would I were stedfast as thou art.
Hello darkness, my old friend.
By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.
Ain't no sunshine when she's gone.

choose.note: Bible: Song of Solomon 3:1, a love song about lying awake at night. 'Thou art' is Keats, not scripture.

options.quote: The night is dark, and I am far from home; lead thou me on!
options.source: John Henry Newman, hymn "Lead, Kindly Light" (1833)

options.quote: Rage, rage against the dying of the light.
options.source: Dylan Thomas, "Do Not Go Gentle into That Good Night" (1951)

options.quote: Turn around, bright eyes.
options.source: Bonnie Tyler, "Total Eclipse of the Heart" (1983)

options.quote: Surely the darkness shall cover me; even the night shall be light about me.

choose.note: Bible: Psalm 139:11. The hymn 'Lead, Kindly Light' sounds older, but it was written in 1833.

options.quote: Here comes the sun.
The winter is past, the rain is over and gone.
I can see clearly now.
options.source: Johnny Nash, "I Can See Clearly Now" (1972)

options.quote: If Winter comes, can Spring be far behind?
options.source: Percy Bysshe Shelley, "Ode to the West Wind" (1820)

choose.note: Bible: Song of Solomon 2:11. The Beatles and Johnny Nash sang about the same moment: winter and rain ending.

options.quote: Rough winds do shake the darling buds of May, and summer's lease hath all too short a date.
In the bleak midwinter, frosty wind made moan.
Seasons in the sun.
The harvest is past, the summer is ended, and we are not saved.

choose.note: Bible: Jeremiah 8:20. It sounds like an indie lyric; the 'hath' line is Shakespeare's Sonnet 18.

options.quote: They have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind.
Like a candle in the wind.
The answer, my friend, is blowin' in the wind.
Blow, winds, and crack your cheeks! rage! blow!
options.source: William Shakespeare, King Lear, Act 3 Scene 2 (c. 1606)

choose.note: Bible: Hosea 8:7, the origin of 'sow the wind, reap the whirlwind'. The rest are Elton John, Bob Dylan and King Lear.

options.quote: Riders on the storm.
The heaven was black with clouds and wind, and there was a great rain.
Into each life some rain must fall, some days must be dark and dreary.
All those moments will be lost in time, like tears in rain.
options.source: Blade Runner (1982), spoken by Roy Batty

choose.note: Bible: 1 Kings 18:45, the rain that ended Elijah's drought. 'Into each life some rain must fall' is Longfellow.

options.quote: He hath loosed the fateful lightning of His terrible swift sword.
options.source: Julia Ward Howe, "Battle Hymn of the Republic" (1862)

options.quote: There's a man goin' 'round takin' names.
Fire and brimstone coming down from the skies! Rivers and seas boiling!
I looked, and behold a pale horse: and his name that sat on him was Death, and Hell followed with him.

choose.note: Bible: Revelation 6:8, the fourth horseman. Johnny Cash's song is about these horsemen; the 'hath' line is the Battle Hymn.

options.quote: Some say the world will end in fire, some say in ice.
This is the way the world ends, not with a bang but a whimper.
I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away; and there was no more sea.
It's the end of the world as we know it.
options.source: R.E.M., "It's the End of the World as We Know It (And I Feel Fine)" (1987)

choose.note: Bible: Revelation 21:1. Frost and Eliot wrote the other famous end-of-the-world lines; R.E.M. sang one.

options.quote: God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying.
Knockin' on heaven's door.
Some glad morning when this life is over, I'll fly away.
options.source: Albert E. Brumley, hymn "I'll Fly Away" (1929)

options.quote: Swift to its close ebbs out life's little day; earth's joys grow dim, its glories pass away.
options.source: Henry Francis Lyte, hymn "Abide with Me" (1847)

choose.note: Bible: Revelation 21:4. The 'earth's joys grow dim' line is the hymn 'Abide with Me' (1847).

options.quote: A hard rain's a-gonna fall.
options.source: Bob Dylan, "A Hard Rain's a-Gonna Fall" (1963)

options.quote: Heaven is a place, a place where nothing, nothing ever happens.
Bad moon rising.
There was silence in heaven about the space of half an hour.

choose.note: Bible: Revelation 8:1, when the seventh seal is opened. The others are Dylan, Talking Heads and Creedence.

options.quote: Gather ye rosebuds while ye may, old time is still a-flying.
options.source: Robert Herrick, "To the Virgins, to Make Much of Time" (1648)

options.quote: A man hath no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be merry.
Let the good times roll.
options.source: Shirley and Lee, "Let the Good Times Roll" (1956)

options.quote: Let us have wine and women, mirth and laughter, sermons and soda-water the day after.
options.source: Lord Byron, Don Juan, Canto II (1819)

choose.note: Bible: Ecclesiastes 8:15, the source of 'eat, drink and be merry'. 'Gather ye rosebuds' is Herrick's 1648 poem.

options.quote: Drink to me only with thine eyes.
A Book of Verses underneath the Bough, a Jug of Wine, a Loaf of Bread, and Thou.
options.source: Edward FitzGerald, The Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam (1859)

options.quote: Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine which I have mingled.
Wine is bottled poetry.
options.source: Robert Louis Stevenson, The Silverado Squatters (1883)

choose.note: Bible: Proverbs 9:5, Wisdom inviting people to her feast. The 'bread, wine and thou' line is the Rubaiyat.

options.quote: With great power comes great responsibility.
Power tends to corrupt, and absolute power corrupts absolutely.
options.source: Lord Acton, letter to Mandell Creighton (1887)

options.quote: I charge thee, fling away ambition: by that sin fell the angels.
options.source: William Shakespeare, Henry VIII, Act 3 Scene 2 (c. 1613)

options.quote: Unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required.

choose.note: Bible: Luke 12:48, the old original of Spider-Man's 'great power, great responsibility'. 'I charge thee' is Shakespeare.

options.quote: What doesn't kill you makes you stronger.
Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit.
You either die a hero, or you live long enough to see yourself become the villain.
options.source: The Dark Knight (2008), spoken by Harvey Dent

options.quote: The price of greatness is responsibility.
options.source: Winston Churchill, speech at Harvard University (1943)

choose.note: Bible: Zechariah 4:6. Kelly Clarkson's line goes back to Nietzsche (1888), not the Bible.

options.quote: My name is Ozymandias, King of Kings; look on my works, ye Mighty, and despair!
I used to rule the world.
Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown.
options.source: William Shakespeare, Henry IV, Part 2, Act 3 Scene 1 (c. 1598)

options.quote: Put not your trust in princes, nor in the son of man, in whom there is no help.

choose.note: Bible: Psalm 146:3. 'King of Kings' sounds biblical, but that line is Shelley's poem 'Ozymandias'.

options.quote: A feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh merry: but money answereth all things.
Money, that's what I want.
Money, so they say, is the root of all evil today.
Put money in thy purse.
options.source: William Shakespeare, Othello, Act 1 Scene 3 (c. 1603), spoken by Iago

choose.note: Bible: Ecclesiastes 10:19. Sounds like a rap line. Pink Floyd's 'root of all evil' echoes 1 Timothy 6:10.

options.quote: Money can't buy me love.
Greed, for lack of a better word, is good.
options.source: Wall Street (1987), spoken by Gordon Gekko

options.quote: Riches certainly make themselves wings; they fly away as an eagle toward heaven.
We are living in a material world.

choose.note: Bible: Proverbs 23:5. Money growing wings and flying off sounds like a pop lyric, but it is a proverb.

options.quote: In this world nothing can be said to be certain, except death and taxes.
options.source: Benjamin Franklin, letter to Jean-Baptiste Le Roy (1789)

options.quote: Money makes the world go around.
options.source: Liza Minnelli and Joel Grey, "Money, Money", from the film Cabaret (1972)

options.quote: Remember that time is money.
options.source: Benjamin Franklin, Advice to a Young Tradesman (1748)

options.quote: Owe no man any thing, but to love one another.

choose.note: Bible: Romans 13:8, Paul's advice on debt. Both Franklin lines sound like proverbs but are his own.

options.quote: Better to remain silent and be thought a fool than to speak and remove all doubt.
options.source: Usually credited to Abraham Lincoln or Mark Twain (doubtful); earliest known similar version by Maurice Switzer (1907)

options.quote: Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise.
Wise men say only fools rush in.
options.source: Elvis Presley, "Can't Help Falling in Love" (1961)

options.quote: Give every man thy ear, but few thy voice.
options.source: William Shakespeare, Hamlet, Act 1 Scene 3 (c. 1600), spoken by Polonius

choose.note: Bible: Proverbs 17:28. The 'remain silent' quote is the same idea; its credit to Lincoln or Twain is doubtful.

options.quote: Stupid is as stupid does.
options.source: Forrest Gump (1994), spoken by Forrest Gump

options.quote: The fool on the hill sees the sun going down.
options.source: The Beatles, "The Fool on the Hill" (1967)

options.quote: A fool and his money are soon parted.
options.source: English proverb; early form in Thomas Tusser, Five Hundred Points of Good Husbandry (1573)

options.quote: A wise man's heart is at his right hand; but a fool's heart at his left.

choose.note: Bible: Ecclesiastes 10:2. Sounds like a joke or a song line, but it is from the Bible.

options.quote: Some books are to be tasted, others to be swallowed, and some few to be chewed and digested.
Of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.
Don't know much about history.
The more that you read, the more things you will know.
options.source: Dr. Seuss, I Can Read with My Eyes Shut! (1978)

choose.note: Bible: Ecclesiastes 12:12. Every student's complaint about homework is in the Bible.

options.quote: Knowledge is power.
options.source: Usually credited to Francis Bacon, from his Latin "ipsa scientia potestas est" (1597)

options.quote: Imagination is more important than knowledge.
options.source: Albert Einstein, interview with George Sylvester Viereck (1929)

options.quote: We don't need no education.
options.source: Pink Floyd, "Another Brick in the Wall, Part 2" (1979)

options.quote: Wisdom is better than strength: nevertheless the poor man's wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.

choose.note: Bible: Ecclesiastes 9:16. Sounds like a protest song about the poor going unheard.

options.quote: Wine is a mocker, strong drink is raging.
Red, red wine, go to my head.
God made beer because he loves us and wants us to be happy.
options.source: Usually credited to Benjamin Franklin (doubtful; he wrote that wine is proof God loves us)

options.quote: I have taken more out of alcohol than alcohol has taken out of me.
options.source: Usually attributed to Winston Churchill; attribution not verified

choose.note: Bible: Proverbs 20:1. The beer line is wrongly credited to Franklin, who wrote about wine.

options.quote: The whiskey drowns and the beer chases my blues away.
We'll tak' a cup o' kindness yet.
Let him drink, and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.
In wine there is truth.
options.source: Latin proverb "in vino veritas"; the idea appears in Pliny the Elder, Natural History, Book 14

choose.note: Bible: Proverbs 31:7. Sounds like a country drinking song, but it is a proverb.

options.quote: Freedom's just another word for nothing left to lose.
You can't handle the truth!
options.source: A Few Good Men (1992), spoken by Col. Nathan Jessup

options.quote: Beauty is truth, truth beauty, that is all ye know on earth, and all ye need to know.
options.source: John Keats, "Ode on a Grecian Urn" (1819)

options.quote: Ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.

choose.note: Bible: John 8:32, Jesus speaking. It is carved in the CIA's lobby, so many think it is a motto.

options.quote: If the Son therefore shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed.
I wish I knew how it would feel to be free.
options.source: Nina Simone, "I Wish I Knew How It Would Feel to Be Free" (1967)

options.quote: The condition upon which God hath given liberty to man is eternal vigilance.
options.source: John Philpot Curran, speech in Dublin (1790)

options.quote: They may take our lives, but they'll never take our freedom!

choose.note: Bible: John 8:36. Curran's 'God hath given liberty' is a 1790 speech, later shortened to 'eternal vigilance'.

options.quote: Life is short, and art long.
options.source: Hippocrates, Aphorisms 1.1 (English translation of "ars longa, vita brevis")

options.quote: What is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away.
Who wants to live forever?
So long as men can breathe or eyes can see, so long lives this, and this gives life to thee.

choose.note: Bible: James 4:14. Hippocrates, Queen and Shakespeare all muse on short lives; only the vapour line is scripture.

options.quote: Only the good die young.
options.source: Billy Joel, "Only the Good Die Young" (1977)

options.quote: Give me liberty, or give me death!
options.source: Patrick Henry, speech to the Virginia Convention (1775), as reported by William Wirt (1817)

options.quote: Do not stand at my grave and weep; I am not there. I do not sleep.
options.source: Mary Elizabeth Frye, "Do not stand at my grave and weep" (1932); authorship long disputed

options.quote: A living dog is better than a dead lion.

choose.note: Bible: Ecclesiastes 9:4. Sounds like a gangster film line, but it is from the Bible.

options.quote: Swing low, sweet chariot, coming for to carry me home.
options.source: "Swing Low, Sweet Chariot", African American spiritual, credited to Wallace Willis (before 1862)

options.quote: The living know that they shall die: but the dead know not any thing.
Don't fear the reaper.
options.source: Blue Oyster Cult, "(Don't Fear) The Reaper" (1976)

options.quote: Get busy living, or get busy dying.
options.source: The Shawshank Redemption (1994), spoken by Andy Dufresne

choose.note: Bible: Ecclesiastes 9:5. Sounds like a goth or metal lyric, but it is from the Bible.

options.quote: I get knocked down, but I get up again.
I won't back down.
A just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again.
Once more unto the breach, dear friends, once more.
options.source: William Shakespeare, Henry V, Act 3 Scene 1 (1599), spoken by King Henry

choose.note: Bible: Proverbs 24:16. Chumbawamba's 'get up again' is the same idea, nearly 3,000 years later.

options.quote: If God be for us, who can be against us?
The only thing we have to fear is fear itself.
options.source: Franklin D. Roosevelt, first inaugural address (1933)

options.quote: Fear is the path to the dark side.
options.source: Star Wars: Episode I - The Phantom Menace (1999), spoken by Yoda

options.quote: We shall fight on the beaches, we shall fight on the landing grounds.
options.source: Winston Churchill, speech to the House of Commons (4 June 1940)

choose.note: Bible: Romans 8:31. It sounds like a battle cry; the beaches line is Churchill in 1940.

options.quote: Lean on me.
Keep your friends close, but your enemies closer.
options.source: The Godfather Part II (1974), spoken by Michael Corleone

options.quote: Those friends thou hast, and their adoption tried, grapple them to thy soul with hoops of steel.
options.source: William Shakespeare, Hamlet, Act 1 Scene 3 (c. 1600), spoken by Polonius

options.quote: Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.

choose.note: Bible: Proverbs 27:17. The 'hoops of steel' line is Polonius in Hamlet, not Scripture.

options.quote: You've got a friend in me.
options.source: Randy Newman, "You've Got a Friend in Me" (1995), from Toy Story

options.quote: Better is a neighbour that is near than a brother far off.
Louis, I think this is the beginning of a beautiful friendship.
I get by with a little help from my friends.
options.source: The Beatles, "With a Little Help from My Friends" (1967)

choose.note: Bible: Proverbs 27:10. Sounds like a country song about good neighbours, but it is a proverb.

options.quote: The path of the righteous man is beset on all sides by the inequities of the selfish and the tyranny of evil men.
options.source: Pulp Fiction (1994), spoken by Jules Winnfield

options.quote: If you build it, he will come.
options.source: Field of Dreams (1989), spoken by the Voice

options.quote: All we have to decide is what to do with the time that is given us.
options.source: J. R. R. Tolkien, The Fellowship of the Ring (1954), spoken by Gandalf

options.quote: I will execute great vengeance upon them with furious rebukes; and they shall know that I am the LORD, when I shall lay my vengeance upon them.

choose.note: Bible: Ezekiel 25:17. Pulp Fiction's 'Ezekiel 25:17' speech is mostly invented; only the ending is close to the verse.

options.quote: Every little thing is gonna be alright.
options.source: Bob Marley and the Wailers, "Three Little Birds" (1977)

options.quote: Don't worry, be happy.
Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
All shall be well, and all shall be well, and all manner of thing shall be well.
options.source: Julian of Norwich, Revelations of Divine Love (c. 1395)

choose.note: Bible: John 14:27, Jesus to his disciples. 'All shall be well' is the medieval mystic Julian of Norwich.

options.quote: Whatever will be, will be.
Don't stop thinking about tomorrow.
Tomorrow, and tomorrow, and tomorrow, creeps in this petty pace from day to day.
Boast not thyself of to morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.

choose.note: Bible: Proverbs 27:1. Doris Day, Fleetwood Mac and Macbeth all talk about tomorrow; only this one is scripture.
